title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: A person who is an employee, officer or director or person seconded to the Liberty Group and includes the Senior Executives; certain contractors where stated in their terms of engagement. Subject to the base rules: Trading only during Trading Windows (absent permission), no short-term trading, no short positions, no hedging of unvested or disposal-restricted employee incentive securities, and insider trading law.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Any director of the Company or the RE. Must give prior written Trading Notice to the Chair (or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair's own trades) and obtain Trade Clearance before Trading even within an open Trading Window; must immediately notify the Company Secretary of all acquisitions, disposals or other Trading without exception; margin lending is prohibited absent Board approval.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: The CEO, COO and CFO; all direct reports to the CEO, COO, CFO or Executive Director; other AASB 124 key management personnel; and any Staff member the Board designates as a Senior Executive. Same Trading Notice/Trade Clearance regime as Directors (Company Secretary as Notification Officer); margin lending prohibited absent Board approval; also subject to the Corporations Act's separate 'closely related parties' remuneration-hedging prohibition.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouses, family members, trusts, companies, nominees and other persons or entities over whom a Director or Senior Executive has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence (also referred to as 'closely related parties' for the Corporations Act remuneration-hedging overlay). Directors and Senior Executives must give at least 5 business days' prior written notice of proposed Trading on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share, option or other Security granted or awarded under an employee incentive scheme (or a vested share, option or other Security granted, awarded or acquired under an employee incentive scheme that is still subject to disposal restrictions).

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chair, in consultation with the Board of the Company and the Board of the RE, may declare a Trading Window closed at any time, at absolute discretion and without prior notice, and may impose an additional Prohibited Period. Refusals of Trade Clearance or of permission to trade under Exceptional Circumstances must be kept confidential by the recipient, but the existence of a general closure is not stated to be confidential.

financing_disclosure: Directors and Senior Executives; trigger: entry into an approved Margin Lending Arrangement; to: Company Secretary; deadline: as soon as practicable, and in any case not more than 24 hours after entry (8.5).

exemption_authority: Exceptional Circumstances permission to trade outside Trading Windows (severe financial hardship, court order/legal requirement, or other exceptional circumstances) is granted entirely at the discretion of the Chair (or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair) after consulting both Boards, valid for 5 trading days unless otherwise specified, with no reasons required and refusal kept confidential (section 7). Separately, the Board of the Company may approve a Margin Lending Arrangement for Directors and Senior Executives (8.3). Neither route extends to the 'short positions' prohibition (3.6(b)), which has no stated exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (short positions) Trading in Securities which enable a Staff member to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This clause has no vesting or tier qualifier, so it independently bans the purchased-put leg of any collar over any Securities (vested or unvested) for every Staff member, making a funded collar impossible under this Policy regardless of approval sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly recognises a 'collar' as a Derivative and therefore a Security in scope; there is no argument that an OTC collar falls outside the Policy's defined terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is excluded from breach only if the underlying secured loan was itself properly Board-approved; an unapproved or informally structured funded facility would leave the bank's enforcement sale in breach of the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Corporations Act prohibits a Senior Executive and their “closely related parties” from entering into arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the Senior Executive’s exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration ... that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a disposal restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a non-waivable statutory prohibition (not merely a Policy rule) that extends to a Senior Executive's spouse, children, dependants and controlled trusts/companies/super funds, so routing the collar through such an entity does not avoid it for unvested or restricted remuneration securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Staff who hold Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to trade in Securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares under ASX or voluntary escrow cannot be collared at all during the escrow period, independent of the vesting analysis.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not possible under this Policy in any form. The 'short positions' rule (3.6(b)) bans, for every Staff member and at every vesting state including fully vested unrestricted shares, any Trading in Securities (expressly including Derivatives, defined to include 'collars') that would let the holder profit from or limit the economic risk of a price decrease - this squarely prohibits the purchased-put leg with no exemption authority reaching it. A narrower, overlapping ban also applies to hedging unvested or disposal-restricted employee incentive securities (3.6(c)), reinforced for Senior Executives and their closely related parties by a non-waivable Corporations Act prohibition (3.7). Even if the put leg were somehow structured to avoid this characterisation, the funding leg (a loan secured on the shares) is only available to Directors and Senior Executives with prior Board approval and 24-hour disclosure, and a lender's enforcement sale loses its exemption from the Trading Window rules if that underlying facility was not properly approved. General Staff face no special margin-lending restriction, but they remain subject to the same absolute short-positions ban, so the structural blocker applies across every tier.
